decision.explanation: Apply C₁ → C₁ − 3C₃, C₂ → C₂ + C₃, and C₄ → C₄ − 2C₃. These preserve the determinant and make row 3 equal to (0,0,1,0). Expanding along that row gives the determinant of [[−4,−5,−8],[5,1,7],[0,−6,0]], which equals 6((−4)(7)−(−8)(5)) = 72.

$\,|\begin{aligned}5 & -8 & 3 & -2 \\ -7 & 5 & -4 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ -6 & -4 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
after.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & -8 & 3 & -2 \\ -7 & 5 & -4 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ -6 & -4 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-3){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-2){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-4 & -5 & 3 & -8 \\ 5 & 1 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-4 & -5 & 3 & -8 \\ 5 & 1 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}-4 & -5 & -8 \\ 5 & 1 & 7 \\ 0 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-4 & -5 & -8 \\ 5 & 1 & 7 \\ 0 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-6)\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =6(-28+40) \\  & =72.\end{aligned}
$$

|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}|

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-3){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-1){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-3){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-1){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{44}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-4){C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 \\ 11 & -3 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 \\ 11 & -3 & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-4){C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -5 & -4 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ -11 & 7 & 9 & -6\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero.*
after.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 2 & 7 \\ 7 & -5 & -4 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ -11 & 7 & 9 & -6\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-2){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & -6 & 15 \\ 2 & -5 & 6 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 7 & -5 & 8\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & -6 & 15 \\ 2 & -5 & 6 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 7 & -5 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 15 \\ 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -4 & -5 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 15 \\ 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -4 & -5 & 8\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
